before: Flex container rules arrange a row; flex item rules decide how each child uses its share of space.
flex-basis gives an item’s starting size along the main axis before free space is distributed.

flex-grow controls how positive free space is shared. Equal grow factors share that free space equally; they do not always imply equal final widths when starting sizes differ.

A flex-grow factor of zero opts that item out of receiving positive extra free space. Positive grow factors determine how the growing items share that space; a zero factor does not mean the item has zero size.
flex-shrink controls shrinking when space is short. Shrink distribution also depends on the starting basis size.

With equal starting bases and equal factors, these simple items stay equal.
```css
.item { flex: 1 1 80px; min-width: 0; }
```
The shorthand order is grow, shrink, basis.
min-width: 0 allows the items to shrink below their usual minimum-content width. In real layouts, still protect readable content from clipping.
The practice has no gaps, padding or borders, so its equal widths isolate item sizing rather than extra box space.
after: A flex container arranges its child elements in a row or column. Each child can have rules for how much space it uses.
`flex-basis` sets an item's starting size. In a row, this is its starting width.

`flex-grow` lets an item use spare space. Two items with the same positive number share the spare space equally. They can still end up different sizes if they started at different sizes. A value of `0` means the item does not grow.
`flex-shrink` lets an item get smaller when the row is too full. The starting size also affects how much each item shrinks.
`min-width: 0` lets a box become narrower than its content would normally allow. Check that the words inside still fit or wrap.
The practice uses two equal boxes with no gaps, padding, or borders. This makes their widths easier to compare.

before.question: Two items have equal bases but flex-grow: 0. The row has spare space. What happens?
choices: The items automatically split all spare space
They do not grow to consume that space
before.explanation: A zero grow factor declines positive free space. Container alignment may position the remaining space, but it does not make these items grow.

after.question: Two items use flex-grow: 0. What happens when the row has spare space?
choices: They grow to fill the spare space
They keep their size instead of growing
after.explanation: A grow value of 0 means the items do not grow to fill spare space.
